title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets' (the loop or hexagon-type relations of the Longue Marche) for U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}. Its symmetry group is the anharmonic group S_3 of Möbius maps permuting {0,1,∞}, extended by complex conjugation: G = S_3 × Z/2, of order 12 (dihedral of order 12). On the previous page he realised the generators geometrically on the Riemann sphere.
- The σ's (with and without tilde) are reflections (anti-holomorphic involutions) in great circles.
- The τ's are involutions.
- ρ is the order-3 rotation z -> 1/(1-z) or its inverse.
He also chose a base point P and paths l. Here he compares this with a second system of generators τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞.

(22) The new generators are:
- τ'_0 = σ̃_∞;
- τ'_1 = σ̃_0;
- τ'_∞ = τ_∞, where τ_∞ = σ_∞σ̃_∞ = σ̃_∞σ_∞ (two commuting reflections).
These are the three reflections in the sides of a geodesic triangle with angles π/2, π/3, 0, read on the base point side. The τ' are the images of the standard Coxeter generators of the extended modular group PGL(2,Z) ≅ GL(2,Z)/{±1}. The next page makes this explicit: GL(2,Z)/±1 = Aut_ext(Π_{0,3}), acting on the Poincaré half-plane.

(23) The defining Coxeter relations of the (2,3,∞) extended triangle group are τ'^2 = 1 for each generator, (τ'_0τ'_∞)^2 = 1 and (τ'_1τ'_0)^3 = 1. There is no relation on τ'_1τ'_∞, which corresponds to the cusp. He checks they hold in G:
- τ'_0τ'_∞ = σ̃_∞σ_∞σ̃_∞ = σ_∞, which has order 2.
- τ'_1τ'_0 = σ̃_0σ̃_∞ = ρ^{-1}, by formula (13) of [C], which has order 3.
So τ'_i ↦ (given elements) defines a homomorphism PGL(2,Z) -> S_3 × Z/2. In modern terms this is reduction mod 2, PSL(2,Z) -> SL(2,F_2) ≅ S_3, extended by the orientation character. It is the level-2 (Legendre λ-line) cover M_{0,4}^{ord} = U_{0,3} -> M_{1,1}, with Γ(2) as kernel on the orientation-preserving part.

(24) The rotation elements, products of two adjacent reflections, are:
- l'_0 = τ'_∞τ'_1 = σ_∞σ̃_∞σ̃_0 = σ_∞ρ (image of the parabolic generator);
- l'_1 = τ'_0τ'_∞ = σ_∞ (image of the order-2 elliptic element);
- l'_∞ = τ'_1τ'_0 = ρ^{-1} (image of the order-3 elliptic element).

(25) These satisfy l'_∞ l'_1 l'_0 = 1, l'_1^2 = 1 and l'_∞^3 = 1. This is the standard presentation PSL(2,Z) = <a,b,c | abc = 1, b^2 = c^3 = 1> ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, with the parabolic element left free. 'Tout est OK!'

Margin. He inverts the dictionary, expressing ρ, the σ's, τ's and l's of G as words in τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞. Examples: ρ = τ'_0τ'_1, τ_0 = ρτ_∞ρ^{-1}, σ_∞ = τ'_0τ'_∞. This shows the τ' generate G. He then lists the ε_i = l'_i.

Purpose. This is bookkeeping that fixes compatible base points and generators. It lets the action of the extended modular group GL(2,Z)/±1 (outer automorphisms of the free group Π_{0,3} preserving the geometry) be matched with the symmetry group of the three-punctured sphere. It is groundwork for writing the loop/hexagon relations for Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on profinite π_1.
errors: No mathematical errors in the main text; all identities check given σ_∞σ̃_∞ = σ̃_∞σ_∞, the involutivity of the reflections, and σ̃_0σ̃_∞ = ρ^{-1} (so σ̃_∞σ̃_0 = ρ).

Several marginal formulas (as transcribed, marked [?]) look garbled or tentative. Example: σ_1 = ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ is rendered with a redundant τ'_0τ'_0. Example: σ_0 is written with σ̃_∞ instead of σ_∞. The final lines are probably ε_i = l'_i rather than τ_i.

ideas.what: Extended modular group PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,∞) Coxeter reflection group generated by three reflections τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group as a hyperbolic triangle reflection group
ideas.where_published: GL(2,Z) acting on Π_{0,3} appears in Esquisse d'un programme; this explicit computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Homomorphism PGL(2,Z) -> S_3 × Z/2 (symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,∞} including complex conjugation), given by reflections mapping to reflections
ideas.modern_name: Reduction mod 2 / level-2 Legendre cover M_{0,4} -> M_{1,1}, extended by complex conjugation

ideas.what: Rotation elements l'_i as products of adjacent reflections, satisfying l'_∞ l'_1 l'_0 = 1, l'_1^2 = l'_∞^3 = 1

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine consistency check of standard presentations (the (2,3,∞) triangle group / PGL(2,Z) mapping onto S_3 × Z/2). It is useful only as bookkeeping within the unpublished 'équation des lacets' project, with no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Opening words 'En visionnant' are likely 'En résumé' or 'En réunissant'. The '(13)' after [C] appears crossed out or parenthetical.
In (22) the annotations are probably '(sur σ̃_∞ i)', '(sur σ̃_0 i)', '(sur i)', i.e. the reflection axes.
Margin: the group is written as Π_1(U_{0,3}) / (S_3 × Z/(2)) or similar, not clearly π_1(M_{0,3}).
The last three marginal lines read ε_0 = l'_0 = τ'_∞τ'_1, ε_1 = τ'_0τ'_∞, ε_∞ = τ'_1τ'_0 (ε, not τ).
Margin σ_0 should be ρσ_∞ρ^{-1}, i.e. σ without tilde.
